records.subject: Checking in on Willow Labs' setup
records.body:
Hi Leo,

Hope the first few days with Wrenfield have been smooth. If you'd like, I can help you set up a first project so you're not starting from a blank page.

Best,
Nadia Goldberg

records.subject: Getting your team organized in Wrenfield
records.body:
Hi Leo,

A quick nudge: Wrenfield works best once your team's actual tasks are in it. If you've been meaning to set that up, today's as good a day as any.

Warmly,
Elena Kelly

records.subject: Getting started with Wrenfield
records.body:
Hi Leo,

Welcome to Wrenfield! Your workspace is ready. A good first step is to create your first project and invite a teammate.

If anything's unclear, just reply here.

Best,
Nadia Goldberg

decisions.rationale: 6 days in with no project, no invite, no key milestone, and zero replies to three touches (email:be1b8023, a59434d2, 36e9c56d) despite an onboarding call held 7/9 (calendar:e82d995a). Pro plan and call attendance show intent, but sustained silence over 8 remaining days makes unaided activation unlikely.

draft.subject: A first project in Wrenfield
draft.body:
Hi Leo,

Thanks again for making time for our onboarding call last week. Since then I haven't wanted to pile on, so just one practical offer: if you send me a sense of how Willow Labs groups its work, I'll help you shape your first project in Wrenfield. Projects are the main organizing unit, and tasks live inside them, and the in-app onboarding flow walks through creating a first project if you'd rather do it yourself. When you're ready for the team, a teammate can be invited from Account Settings -> Members at any time.

Best,
Nadia
